description: A small, readable UCI chess engine in Rust, written to be picked up and adapted: a two-thread UCI shell (the stdin loop keeps answering while a search thread thinks) with pluggable move-selection strategies
rules: Install with: cargo install anglerfry. Run the binary and type uci; point any chess GUI at it as a UCI engine (no arguments, no working directory).
It plays weakly on purpose: the value is the protocol shape, not the moves. The Strategy UCI option selects how moves are picked (random, two-ply).

To build your own engine from it: clone the repository and add a strategy file under src/strategy/ implementing pick(board, limits); the README's 'Add a strategy' section lists the two-line registration.
The source is the documentation: src/uci/ is the protocol loop and parser, src/search.rs the time/depth/node budgeting and the search thread, src/strategy/ the move selection examples.
Set RUST_LOG=debug for a stderr trace of every command handled and ignored.
Conformance is verified with uci-test-suite (uvx uci-test-suite ./target/release/anglerfry); it passes every level it declares.
